name: Expert Interviewer rubric
source_document: Final Rubric Summary, with its tracked edits accepted
purpose: Score the interviewer on whether they conducted an interview that developed reliable, usable information, properly managed the witness, and facilitated the interview in accordance to their ethical obligations.

rating_scale.0: Missing: no meaningful demonstration despite a fair opportunity.
rating_scale.1: Weak: recognizes the issue minimally or attempts the skill ineffectively.
rating_scale.2: Adequate: demonstrates the basic skill, but incompletely or inconsistently.
rating_scale.3: Strong: uses the skill effectively in the relevant opportunities.
rating_scale.4: Excellent: uses the skill consistently, strategically, and adaptively.

scoring_method: Compare what the person actually said in the interview with each skill's description and the 0-4 rating scale. The rating decides how much of that skill's marks the person gets: marks = skill marks x rating / 4 (4 gets all of it, 2 gets half, 0 gets none).

areas.name: Interview Framing, Rapport Building, & Closing
areas.checks: Did they say "I work for the company, not for you" at the start, and close properly at the end?

skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.

areas.name: Question Technique
areas.checks: Did they let the witness talk first and ask clear questions?

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing
areas.checks: Did they ask follow-up questions when an answer was vague?

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.

areas.name: Document Use
areas.checks: Did they show the documents fairly and let the witness explain?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.

areas.no_document_rule: If no document was provided, these marks are not taken away: the person receives them in full.

fair_scoring_rules: The witness's behaviour never influences the scoring. An easy witness doesn't mean a high score, and a hard one doesn't mean a low score.
Every score needs proof from what was actually said in the interview.
If no document was provided, the tool doesn't take away marks. If a document was provided and the person didn't use it, they lose marks.

score_caps.mistake: No warning about whom the lawyer represents before the questions start and/or fails to explain privilege.
Telling the employee the lawyer represents them, or that they control privilege.
Changing or misquoting what a document says.

score_caps_rule: These caps only apply when there is clear proof in the interview or the document.
upjohn_warning: The lawyer should explain: the company is the client; the lawyer is not the employee's personal lawyer; the company controls privilege and may share what is said; and the employee can ask questions. It must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
validity_conditions: The whole interview is available, from start to finish. An interview that ended early still counts; how it's graded depends on who ended it (see ending_rules).
The case gave the lawyer a relevant document and a fair chance to use it.
There was a gap or a challenge in the witness's story to work with.
The witness had a consistent hidden personality and a fixed set of case facts.

results.label: Scored
results.when: Everything needed was there; a normal score is given.

results.label: Incomplete
results.when: The interviewer ended the interview early, before the case's key issues were reached, or the tool failed to give the lawyer a document, a contradiction or a dodge to work with. Only the part that was reached is rated. This is not a zero for the lawyer.

results.label: Not enough evidence
results.when: Part of the interview is missing (such as its beginning), the document can't be opened, or the case facts contradict each other.

results.label: Safety stop
results.when: Someone asks for real legal advice, research on a real person, or uses real client files. The tool should stop and send them to a supervisor.

score_report: The result: Scored, Incomplete, Not enough evidence or Safety stop.
The rating and marks for each skill, the total for each area and the overall score.
Any big mistakes found, and the final score after any cap.
The exact moments in the interview that back up each area's score, saying which are direct quotes and which are summaries.
Up to two important missed chances, only if they really happened.
Two practical tips, written as better questions to ask next time.

witness_types.behaves: Self-assured senior executive; answers with authority, sometimes beyond what they actually know; bristles when challenged and minimizes anything pointing to their own wrongdoing
witness_types.good_lawyer: Tests each claim (how they know it, which document shows it, who handled the details) and pins down exactly what they knew, approved and when, keeping a respectful tone

witness_types.behaves: Reluctant or adverse; answers exactly the question asked in as few words as possible, meets vague questions with vague answers, and volunteers nothing
witness_types.good_lawyer: Asks narrow, one-fact questions in a logical order, doesn't let a vague answer stand, and stays neutral without rising to the wit

witness_types.behaves: Friendly but not very helpful; rambles about minor details, needs reminding of some facts, and may pass over important ones
witness_types.good_lawyer: Puts them at ease, steers rambling answers back, and uses dates, documents and names to jog their memory

witness_types_rule: The witness type is kept hidden until the end and never affects the score on its own.
tool_tests: A full warning vs. a missing warning: the missing warning must trigger the cap.
A strong vs. a weak interview of the same case: the strong one must score higher, for the right reasons.
A guarded vs. a cooperative witness: no automatic penalty for a difficult witness.
A document that conflicts with the witness: correct use gets credit; misquoting is flagged.
A wrong file or a request for real legal advice: the tool must stop or redirect, not give a normal score.
An interview missing its beginning: the tool must say "not enough evidence," not assume the warning was skipped.
Someone asking the witness to reveal its hidden personality early: it must stay hidden until the end.
An interview the witness ends: a normal score, no penalty for what wasn't reached, never Incomplete.
An interview the interviewer ends early: Incomplete, rating only what was reached.
An interview the interviewer ends late, with topics or the close undone: a normal score, with low ratings in the skills affected.
tool_targets: It misses no big mistakes and flags none that didn't happen.
At least 80% of its skill ratings are within one step of an investigations lawyer's rating.
It ranks at least 90% of strong vs. weak interview pairs correctly.
Every interview moment it cites really exists, and it never makes up documents, quotes or admissions.
It stops or redirects every real-advice or confidential-data request.

interview_outline.use: Reference language for what a well-run interview covers. It is a guide, not a script: don't require its exact wording or order, and remember Adaptability rewards departing from the outline when the witness's answers call for it.
upjohn_warning: The company has retained counsel to investigate the concerns that have been raised; the purpose of the interview is to learn the facts so counsel can give legal advice to the company.
Counsel represents the company only, not the witness personally; counsel is not the witness's attorney and cannot give the witness legal advice.
The interview is confidential and privileged, but the privilege belongs to the company, not to the witness or to counsel.
The company decides whether to waive the privilege and may disclose what is learned, without the witness's consent and without telling them.
The witness should be fully open and truthful, and should not share the substance of the interview with anyone.
interview_outline.ground_rules: Explain the interview ground rules: speculation, assumptions, estimates, and asking for clarification.
sections: Background: position, tenure, prior roles, responsibilities, reporting lines, who they work with, credentials, outside employment or companies.

Background on processes: how the relevant process works from beginning to end, who initiates, reviews, approves and decides, whether it is documented, exceptions, and whether it worked differently in the relevant period.
The specific issue: an open invitation ('Tell me everything you remember'), then what happened next, who else was involved, conversations, and anything unusual.
Chronology: when and how they first learned of it, who was present, what was said, who they told, what was decided and by whom.
Decision-making and responsibility: who was responsible, their own role and recommendation, alternatives considered, who ultimately decided, and where it is documented.
If the witness attributes a decision to someone else: what that person did, whether the witness was told directly or how they know, and who might know more.
Addressing inconsistencies: restate the earlier and current statements, ask the witness to reconcile them, whether their recollection changed and why, and which reflects their present recollection.

Documents: before showing a document, ask what they remember about the subject; then ask whether they recognize it, what it is, when they saw it and its purpose; let them review it; ask what it means to them; then restate their earlier answer and describe the document accurately and neutrally before asking them to explain any difference.

Wrap-up: anything else they think counsel should know, helpful documents, other witnesses; a confidentiality reminder, record retention, not to speak with other witnesses; and, if applicable, an anti-retaliation reminder.

ending_rules: The witness ended it (walked out, stopped to get a lawyer, refused to go on): a normal score, never Incomplete. Rate each skill on what the interviewer did with the chances they had. A skill that never came up because the witness left gets full marks: the interviewer isn't punished for what the witness prevented. This applies to parts of a skill too: if the witness left before the close, judge Closing only on what the interviewer could still say as the witness was leaving, and don't fault closing questions (anything else, other witnesses, other documents) or a lead the interviewer could still have returned to before the end.
The interviewer ended it early, before the case's key issues were reached (for example after only the opening and background): Incomplete. Rate only the skills that came up; the rest are not rated.

The interviewer ended it late, after most key issues were reached but with topics, documents or the close left undone: a normal score, with low ratings in the skills affected (for example Closing, Material Facts, Other Sources, Other Evidence, or the document skills).
The interview ran to its end: grade it normally.
